_comment: 'Connect Agent runs as a sidecar in the ECS task. Customer workloads dial
127.0.0.1 ... Security-group templates in the install bundle must allow
task-to-sidecar local dial and deny cross-task dial to Agent ports.'
ECS tasks on awsvpc networking share one ENI/security-group per task, so
there is no cross-container SG boundary to write within a single task —
127.0.0.1 dial between containers in the same task is unconditionally
allowed by the network namespace itself and cannot be blocked by an SG.
What an SG *can* and must do is deny any OTHER task's ENI from reaching
this task's Agent ports over the VPC network, which is what the ingress
rule below encodes: only this task's own SG (loopback-equivalent at the
SG-membership level) may reach the Agent ports; no other source is listed.
The full ecs-task-definition.json (sidecar container spec, port
publishing) remains blocked on L3-POC-ECS (idle-timeout / task-recycle
PoC in L2-Design.docx §H.8) — this SG template ships independently
because it answers a different question (network ACL) than the PoC
(yamux keepalive survival under Fargate's idle/recycle behavior).
GroupDescription: connect-agent-REPLACE_TENANT — deny cross-task dial to Agent ports

SecurityGroupIngress._comment: Self-referencing rule: only ENIs already in this SG may dial these ports.

SecurityGroupEgress._comment: Outbound-only to the Gateway (Developer-Reference: 'Outbound-only to the Gateway address remains mandatory').
